The initial number of coins is 7 times the number in each of the seven bags, say \(x\) coins per bag, so total = \(7x\). After finding a bag of 53 coins, total = \(7x + 53\). This total must be divisible by 8 to redistribute equally into 8 bags. Also, total > 200.

We have \(7x + 53 \equiv 0 \pmod{8}\), i.e., \(7x \equiv -53 \equiv 3 \pmod{8}\). Since \(7 \equiv -1 \pmod{8}\), this gives \(-x \equiv 3 \pmod{8}\) so \(x \equiv 5 \pmod{8}\). Thus \(x = 8k + 5\) for some integer \(k \ge 0\). Then total = \(7(8k+5)+53 = 56k+88 > 200\) implies \(56k > 112\) so \(k > 2\), hence \(k \ge 3\). The smallest \(k = 3\) gives initial total = \(56\cdot3 + 35 = 203\) (since \(7x = 56k+35\)).

Thus the smallest number of coins before finding the bag is 203.

Answer: 203
